clos.original_description: Understanding how search engines work: Students should be able to explain the underlying technology behind search engines, including the algorithms used to crawl, index and rank web pages.
clos.enriched_description: Understanding how search engines work: Students should be able to explain the underlying technology behind search engines, including the algorithms used to crawl, index and rank web pages. The scope includes Search engineers; Other Search Applications 3; Building blocks: Text acquisition, Text transformation, Index Creattion; Crawling the Web: Retrieving web pages, web crawler, freshness, Crawling, deep web, sitemaps, distributed; Crawling the Web : Crawling, deep web, sitemaps, distributed crawling; Ranking with indexes; Inverted Indexes: documents, counts, positions, fields and extents, scores, ordering; Index construction: simple construction, merging, parallelism and distribution, update; Query processing : structured queries, distributed evaluation, caching, Impact Ordering, static index pruning; Showing the results: result pages and snippets, advertising and search, clustering the results; Fundamentals of Search Engine Optimization: Content, Architecture, HTML, Trust, Links, User-Related Factors; and User Tags and Manual Indexing: Searching Tags, Inferring Missing Tags,Browsing and Tag Clouds.

clos.original_description: Search engine optimization: Students should be able to apply best practices for optimizing web pages to improve their visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs).
clos.enriched_description: Search engine optimization: Students should be able to apply best practices for optimizing web pages to improve their visibility in search engine results pages (SERPs). The scope includes Fundamentals of Search Engine Optimization: Content, Architecture, HTML, Trust, Links, User-Related Factors and The Position of Search Engine Providers.

clos.original_description: Keyword research: Students should be able to conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models..
clos.enriched_description: Keyword research: Students should be able to conduct keyword research to identify the most relevant and profitable keywords by using popular retrieval models.. The scope includes Crawling the Web: Retrieving web pages, web crawler, freshness, Crawling, deep web, sitemaps, distributed; Crawling the Web : Crawling, deep web, sitemaps, distributed crawling; Conversion problem: character encodings; Storing the documents: using database system, random access, compression and large files, update, big table; From Words to Terms; Text statistics; Link analysis: anchor text, pagerank, link quality; Inverted Indexes: documents, counts, positions, fields and extents, scores, ordering; Index construction: simple construction, merging, parallelism and distribution, update; Query processing : structured queries, distributed evaluation, caching, Impact Ordering, static index pruning; Showing the results: result pages and snippets, advertising and search, clustering the results; and Training, testing and statistics: significance tests, setting parameter values, Online testing.

clos.original_description: Analytics and tracking: Students should be able to use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance.
clos.enriched_description: Analytics and tracking: Students should be able to use analytics tools to track website traffic, user behavior, and campaign performance. The scope includes Ranking with indexes; Abstract model of raking; Inverted Indexes: documents, counts, positions, fields and extents, scores, ordering; b Implementing Inverted Indices; Compression : compression in practice, looking ahead, skipping and skip pointers; Index construction: simple construction, merging, parallelism and distribution, update; Query processing : structured queries, distributed evaluation, caching, Impact Ordering, static index pruning; Probabilistic models: Information retrieval as classification, BM25 Ranking Algorithm; Training, testing and statistics: significance tests, setting parameter values, Online testing; Classification and clustering; classification: Navie bayes, Support vector machines, Evaluation, Classfier and feature selection, spam; and Clustering: Hierachical and K-meas clustering, K-nearest neighbor clustering, evaluation, how to choose K.

clos.original_description: Solving problems: Students should be able to apply search engine techniques to solve the real-life problems
clos.enriched_description: Solving problems: Students should be able to apply search engine techniques to solve the real-life problems. The scope includes User Tags and Manual Indexing: Searching Tags, Inferring Missing Tags,Browsing and Tag Clouds; Searching with Communities: What Is a Community?, Finding Communities, Community-Based Question Answering; and Peer-to-Peer and Metasearch: Distributed Search, P2P Networks.
